findings.title: $__range detection runs on interpolated expr, so range-variable queries are now split
findings.body: `runSplitQuery` now calls `applyTemplateVariables` on every query before partitioning. `querySupportsSplitting()` then calls `isQueryWithRangeVariable(query.expr)` on the result. That function looks for the literal `$__range` text, which `templateSrv.replace` has already substituted, so the check no longer matches. Queries using `$__range`/`$__range_s`/`$__range_ms` will be split into daily chunks. As the code comment explains, those queries must not be split. Each chunk then evaluates a range-sized window and the merged result is wrong (e.g. `count_over_time(...[$__range])` summed over chunks). Run the splitting check on the raw target expression before interpolation, or keep the original expr around for it.

findings.title: Queries are interpolated and ad-hoc filters applied multiple times
findings.body:
The splitter now calls `datasource.applyTemplateVariables(query, request.scopedVars, request.filters)`. The sub-requests then go through `datasource.runQuery` (DataSourceWithBackend.query), which calls `applyTemplateVariables` again on each target with the same `filters`. In the sharding path it happens three times: `runShardSplitQuery`, then `runSplitQuery`, then the backend query. The test now asserts 5 calls.

Re-applying ad-hoc filters can add duplicate label matchers or filter stages. Re-interpolating an already interpolated expression can expand `$`-sequences that came from variable values, and can double-escape regex-escaped values. Interpolate once, or strip `filters`/scopedVars from the sub-request so later stages don't re-apply them.

findings.title: Empty-expr filter now runs before interpolation
findings.body: Previously `interpolateVariablesInQueries` ran first and the `query.expr` filter ran on the interpolated result. Now the filter runs on the raw expr and interpolation happens afterwards. A query whose expr is just a variable that resolves to an empty string is no longer dropped and gets sent for execution and sharding. The same ordering applies in `runSplitQuery`. Filter on the interpolated expr instead.
